Objective: Frictionless daily deploy - one command, zero human intervention
Why it matters: The repo must be releasable at a daily pace. Every manual step (env flags, stale-binary workarounds, artifact babysitting) is toil that compounds and blocks the nightly cadence.
Definition of done: A single invocation (`just deploy` with no extra flags, or a CI/CD pipeline on push to main) takes the repo from HEAD to live on Fly, including build, migrations, image push and health verification - with no prompts, no env-var incantations, and a non-zero exit on any failure.
Current state (2026-08-26): `FETCH_ALLOW_MISSING=1 just deploy` works end to end (~20 min) but is not clean: (1) the macOS bridge artifact has never been published, forcing the env flag; (2) the build recipe runs migrations with the PREVIOUS binary, so any config-schema change from a core bump bricks the first deploy after it (hit twice on 2026-08-25); (3) no post-deploy health gate - the app 503s for ~2 min during boot and nothing verifies it came back.
Gap / next action: 1) Bake FETCH_ALLOW_MISSING semantics into the recipe (warn, do not fail, on never-published optional artifacts) or publish the macOS artifact once. 2) Reorder the recipe: build the binary FIRST, then migrate with the binary just built. 3) Append a health-check wait + smoke curl set to `just deploy` so the command exits green only when the site answers 200. 4) Then decide: keep it a local one-liner or lift into CI/CD (GitHub Actions on main) - CI/CD also removes the 'whose machine' problem.
Metric tracked nightly: Deploy: command count to live; wall-clock minutes; manual interventions required; deploy exit reflects real health (Y/N)
Latest value: 1 command + 1 env flag; ~20 min; 0-2 interventions depending on core drift; exit does NOT reflect health

Objective: Gateway latency overhead measured and bounded
Why it matters: Every governed call transits systemprompt compute (auth, governance chain, quota, safety scan, audit write). That adds milliseconds per request; if the overhead is material it degrades every client flow, and today nobody knows the number.
Definition of done: A nightly-published measurement of gateway overhead: p50/p95/p99 of (total request latency minus upstream provider latency) on production traffic, plus a synthetic probe for quiet nights - with an agreed budget (proposed: p95 overhead <= 150ms buffered, <= 50ms to first streamed byte) and an alert when a deploy regresses it.
Current state (2026-08-26): Raw material exists: ai_requests.latency_ms per request, p50/p95 in the dashboard, hourly anomaly detection on latency-adjacent metrics. But total latency conflates provider time with gateway time - upstream duration is not recorded separately, so the OVERHEAD is currently unmeasurable. The newly enabled governance chain + safety scanners (2026-08-25) added stages whose cost has not been quantified.
Gap / next action: 1) Record upstream_latency_ms alongside latency_ms in the audit row (start/stop around the provider call) - small core change; overhead = difference. 2) Add a nightly synthetic probe job (fixed small prompt through the gateway AND direct to provider, delta = overhead) so quiet days still produce the number. 3) Surface overhead p50/p95/p99 on the spend/latency dashboard and in this sheet; alert on regression past the agreed budget. 4) Agree the budget with Astound.
Metric tracked nightly: Gateway overhead ms: p50 / p95 / p99 (production + synthetic probe); regression vs previous night
